summary: Word of Yahweh second time to Jonah: Arise go to Nineveh great city and preach message I give you. Jonah arises goes, Nineveh was exceedingly great city three days' journey. Enters one day's journey crying Yet forty days and Nineveh shall be overthrown. People believe God, proclaim fast, put sackcloth from greatest to least, king of Nineveh rises from throne, covers with sackcloth, sits in ashes, decrees man and beast fast, cry mightily to God, turn from evil, who knows God may turn and relent. God sees they turned from evil way, relents of disaster he said he would do, does not do it.
whyItMatters: Shortest and most effective sermon in Bible — 5 Hebrew words 'Yet forty days Nineveh overthrown' leads to city-wide repentance from king to cattle. Shows mercy to enemies, and God relenting when people turn. Satirical that pagan city repents at Jonah's minimal sermon while Israel often doesn't at longer prophets.

keyVerses.text: Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”
but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and let them cry mightily to God. Yes, let them turn everyone from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.
keyVerses.why: Who knows — hope in God's freedom to relent, not presumption.

keyVerses.text: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way. God relented of the disaster which he said he would do to them, and he didn’t do it.
keyVerses.why: God sees turning, relents — mercy triumphs.

questions.question: Why does Nineveh repent at such short sermon?
questions.answer: Jonah's sermon in Hebrew is just 5 words: Od arba'im yom weNineveh nehpakhet — Yet forty days Nineveh overthrown. Minimal, no call to repent. Yet Ninevites believe God (v5), fast, sackcloth from greatest to least. Irony: Israel hears many prophets at length and doesn't turn; enemy city turns at minimal warning. Shows readiness or desperation — they take threat seriously.

questions.question: What does king in ashes and man and beast fast mean?
questions.answer: King rises from throne, removes robe, covers sackcloth, sits in ashes — symbols of mourning and repentance and abdication of status. Decree that man and beast, herd and flock, taste nothing, covered sackcloth, cry mightily — even animals included, showing total city repentance, creation groaning. Common ancient practice: animals in mourning too.

questions.question: What does 'Who knows whether God will not turn and relent' mean?
questions.answer: Who knows — mi yodea — is not presumption but hope in God's freedom. Joel 2 uses same phrase: who knows if he will not turn. Not claiming to control God, but hoping God is merciful and may relent from anger. Keeps repentance humble — we turn and hope, not demand. God does relent, showing character is to relent from disaster when people turn.

questions.question: Does God change mind? Does relenting contradict immutability?
questions.answer: Verse 10 says God relented of disaster said he would do. Some see divine repentance (nacham) — God responsive, not rigid. Theological debate: does God change or human change triggers different response within consistent character? Jonah's theology says God is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, relenting from disaster (4:2) — so relenting is consistent with merciful character. Mercy triumphs over judgment when turning occurs.

glossary.def: Five Hebrew words — shortest effective sermon, deadline and doom.
Humble hope — who knows whether God may turn and relent, not presumption.
Signs of mourning, repentance, humiliation — king abdicating status.
